source.title: What do larger image classifiers memorise?
source.authors: Michal Lukasik; Vaishnavh Nagarajan; A. S. Rawat; A. Menon; Sanjiv Kumar

record.tranche_reason: The study measures stability-based, example-level memorisation across model sizes and under distillation. It mentions random-label fitting only as background and does not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on a related construct: the Feldman stability-based memorisation score. Those findings are recorded with versions ["none"]. Random-label fitting statements are background or citations, not this study's results. The paper also reports clean-label train/test accuracies, but these do not test the random-label behavior in V1.
record.test_reason: The study measures stability-based per-example memorisation across model sizes and distillation settings, rather than fitting random labels. Random-label interpolation and clean-before-noisy learning are discussed as prior findings. Its own trajectories vary model capacity, not training time, and test none of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Stability-based memorisation exhibits diverse trajectories across model sizes and increasingly bimodal distributions; its average can decrease after interpolation. Distillation tends to reduce this memorisation, especially for examples with increasing capacity trajectories. The proposed explanation for improved generalization is an interpretation of these results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Feldman stability-based per-example memorisation score and its subsampling estimator to study model-size trends and distillation; it does not reproduce random-label fitting experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model family/depth affect the reported average and distributional trends. The paper reports that distillation inhibition is especially pronounced for highly memorised examples and wider teacher-student gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: Average stability-based memorisation decreases beyond a model-size threshold on CIFAR-100 but increases across the tested ImageNet MobileNets; score distributions become more bimodal with model size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model capacity changes the average and distribution of stability-based per-example memorisation in dataset-dependent ways.

fits_no_version.finding: C-score proxy and prediction-depth distributions fail to reproduce the bimodality of stability-based memorisation scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlation with stability-based memorisation does not ensure that a proxy captures its distributional trends.

fits_no_version.finding: Distillation reduces stability-based memorisation, particularly for highly memorised examples and examples whose scores increase with model capacity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Knowledge distillation selectively inhibits stability-based per-example memorisation on image-classification datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Deeper ResNets achieve higher clean-label CIFAR-100 training and test accuracies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested deeper ResNets interpolate clean CIFAR-100 while improving test accuracy.

record.problems: The study uses a computationally expensive subsampling approximation to the stability-based score, with K=400 and M=⌈0.7N⌉; the authors describe a tradeoff between breadth and precision. The study is limited to image classification. Many findings are presented in figures without numeric estimates in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows beyond those listed. Numerous per-example plots and appendix distributions are not separately enumerated; they do not test any listed claim version, and many provide figure-only values.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Interpolation of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
A label-corruption sweep measuring perfect training fit and steadily worsening test performance.
Random-label fitting with weight decay, dropout or augmentation, and clean-label generalization after removing them.
Training-time evidence that shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Naturally ambiguous or mislabeled examples do not constitute a random-label experiment. Gaussian perturbations in Appendix I measure robustness, not fitting Gaussian-noise inputs as specified by V3. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6, rather than denials of the reported findings.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not train on random labels or report test error at chance. Its clean-label train/test results do not test random-label fitting.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across label corruption levels.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep over random-label corruption fractions or corresponding train/test errors.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevents random-label fitting or affects clean-label generalization in the stated comparison.
The paper does not measure training trajectories for real versus random labels; discussion of prior work is not a result from this study.

rows.subject: ResNet models
rows.operation_detail: Compared average stability-based memorisation score across model depths on CIFAR-100.

conditions.value: average memorisation score across training samples

rows.value: The score increases up to depth 20, and then starts decreasing (albeit slightly).
rows.note: This is the paper's stability-based notion of per-example memorisation, not random-label fitting.
rows.check: The reported average-score trend is supported, but stability-based memorisation on standard datasets cannot establish any listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet models
rows.size_stated: ResNet depths on ImageNet; exact depths not stated in the cited result text
rows.operation_detail: Compared average stability-based memorisation score across model depths on ImageNet.
rows.value: Memorisation steadily increases; in-sample accuracy does not saturate.
rows.note: Authors attribute the increase to in-sample accuracy increasing faster than out-of-sample accuracy.
rows.check: Figure 2's ImageNet models are MobileNet models with scale factors 0.35, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 and 1.25, not ResNets of varying depth. The stability-score increase does not measure random-label fitting.

rows.subject: ResNet and MobileNet models
rows.size_stated: Multiple depths and widths; exact list varies by dataset and family
rows.operation_detail: Compared distributions of stability-based memorisation scores across model sizes.
rows.measure: Distribution of per-example stability-based memorisation scores
rows.value: Scores tend to be bi-modal; larger models have a higher fraction of samples with scores close to both 0 and 1. Authors report this across datasets and architectures.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative result across the stated datasets and model families; distinct from the claim's random-label memorisation.
rows.check: The distributional finding concerns stability-based scores, not random-label interpolation or learning order during training.

rows.subject: ResNet models
rows.operation_detail: Grouped CIFAR-100 examples by stability-based memorisation-score trajectory across model sizes.

conditions.value: change less than 0.1 treated as no change

rows.measure: Fraction of examples in each trajectory category
rows.value: At α=0.1: constant 0.395; increasing 0.298; decreasing 0.105; cap-shaped 0.187; other 0.016.
rows.note: These are stability-based score trajectories, not label-noise training trajectories.
rows.check: Table 2 values at alpha=0.10 are correctly recorded. These trajectories run across model sizes, not training iterations, and cannot test V6.

rows.subject: ResNet models
rows.size_stated: ResNet depths; specific values not stated for this comparison
rows.operation_detail: Compared stability-based memorisation score distributions with the C-score proxy cprox and prediction depth.
rows.value: The cprox and prediction-depth marginals are unimodal, unlike the bi-modal stability-based memorisation distribution.
rows.note: A result about proxies for the paper's stability-based measure.
rows.check: This compares distributions of memorisation metrics and proxies; none measures a listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet models
rows.size_stated: CIFAR-100 ResNet student depths; teacher ResNet-110
rows.operation_detail: Compared students trained by logit-matching distillation with one-hot-trained models.
rows.value: Distillation tends to reduce the number of memorised samples; in-sample accuracy becomes lower and out-of-sample accuracy becomes higher.
rows.note: Authors report the effect qualitatively; Figure 5 contains the plotted averages.
rows.check: This is a distillation-versus-one-hot comparison of stability-based scores on standard labels. It does not test whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting.

rows.subject: ResNet students distilled from a ResNet-110 teacher
rows.operation_detail: Compared each student's per-example stability-based memorisation under distillation and one-hot training.

conditions.value: joint density of student and distilled memorisation scores

rows.value: Distillation inhibits memorisation particularly for examples highly memorised by the one-hot model, especially when the teacher-student gap is wide.
rows.note: Authors also state that examples with small one-hot memorisation scores do not obtain a significant increase under distillation.
rows.check: Reduced stability-based memorisation under distillation does not establish any listed random-label or temporal-learning claim.

rows.subject: ResNet-32 student distilled from ResNet-110
rows.operation_detail: Classified examples whose memorisation score decreases under distillation by their one-hot trajectory category.
rows.measure: Fraction of reduced-memorisation examples by trajectory type
rows.baseline: All examples: constant 0.243; increasing 0.175; decreasing 0.145; cap-shaped 0.316; other 0.121.
rows.value: Reduced memorisation: constant 0.000; increasing 0.972; decreasing 0.000; cap-shaped 0.023; other 0.005.
rows.note: Authors say the examples with reduced memorisation are mostly increasing in their trajectory.
rows.check: Table 3 proportions are correctly recorded, but increasing refers to model capacity, not learning later in training.

rows.subject: ResNet models
rows.size_stated: ResNet-8, ResNet-14, ResNet-20, ResNet-32, ResNet-44, ResNet-56, ResNet-110
rows.operation_detail: Reported clean-label CIFAR-100 train and test accuracy across model depths.
rows.note: Clean-label performance only; it does not test the random-label behavior specified in V1.
rows.check: Table 5 accuracies are correctly recorded. Clean-label interpolation with regularization present does not test random-label fitting or the consequences of removing regularization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
